messages.subject_clean: Invitation: Apply to be a Mentoring Organization for GCI
messages.body_plain:
Is R interested?

As I have a lot on my plate right now, I don't think I can volunteer as either mentor or
admin. myself, but would be willing to fill in the form. I think, however, we should have
a team of 4-6 folk who would be involved if we are to do this. And the time-line for
developing tasks for the 13-17 year olds is very short.

JN

-------- Original Message --------
Subject: 	Invitation: Apply to be a Mentoring Organization for GCI
Date: 	Mon, 17 Oct 2011 11:26:48 -0700
From: 	Carol Smith <car...@google.com>
To: 	Google Summer of Code Mentors List <google-summer-of-...@googlegroups.com>

Hi everyone,

Starting today we are accepting applications from organizations who have participated in a
previous Google Summer of Code (you!) to get involved with our contest for 13-17 year
olds, Google Code-in [0] (GCI).

If you havenï¿½t read up about GCI, you can check out our announcement [1] to this list from
Friday or read our blog post [2] about the contest.

If your org has decided it would like to apply to participate in the contest, you can fill
out the application [3] on Melange now. The deadline for applications is 1 November at
23:00 UTC.

Please read over the rules for participating as an organization in GCI before applying,
they can be found on the organization application [3] itself. Please remember to also read
over our Information Page [4] for GCI org admins and mentors to make sure your org has the
time and capacity to participate this year. We have made a couple changes to the workflow
and the task management this year; please make sure you're familiar with them.

We value your orgï¿½s past service to Google Summer of Code, and hope your org will consider
participating in Google Code-in.

[0] - http://code.google.com/gci
[1] - http://groups.google.com/group/google-summer-of-code-mentors-list/msg/9743e65835dab92f
[2] - http://google-opensource.blogspot.com/2011/10/google-code-in-are-you-in.html
[3] -
[4] - http://code.google.com/p/google-code-in/wiki/GCIAdminMentorInformation

Cheers,
Carol

--

messages.body_plain:
John,

I think I could be the admin. I've got a bunch of grad students who might be willing to help me out if I get stuck, and also help participants.
The time line is very short - sorry only just read your email after seeing Claudia's - so it's going to be tough getting the word out. And the timing academically is awkward, mid-semester, but I really feel that participating is really worthwhile for the R community. It could be quite a big deal to get teenagers involved with R.

What would be the next steps, supposing that I am able to be admin, and Claudia one mentor? Who makes the Google contact? There are a few people that I'd try to pull in to be mentors.

cheers,
Di

On Mon, Oct 24, 2011 at 8:51 AM, John C Nash <nas...@uottawa.ca> wrote:
>
> So I think the first step is to see if you can access the registration page.

I can.

> Then we need to fill in the form, and gather some projects. I think they need to be short
> and very doable. I'd suggest things we
> feel would take about a day of our time and not much more.

I'd like to suggest the regression theme in the Nobel Prize in
Economics this year, awarded for "for their empirical research on
cause and effect in the macroeconomy," to the authors of
http://research.mpls.frb.fed.us/research/wp/wp55.pdf -- would OCR and
typing that bitmapped report in R notation, transcribing the tables,
etc., be a suitable documentation task?  Similarly, the principal
component analysis in
http://motherjones.com/mojo/2011/10/study-income-inequality-kills-economic-growth
is another timely documentation task which would probably interest
teens.  It could be easy or medium, depending on whether they want to
put in a few examples to illustrate.

Should I suggest that my GSOC tasks dismissed as two easy be included?

Regards,
James S.

I could be either an admin or a mentor. I have some colleagues teaching

very young students. I could do the translations myself so we could
potentially involve all Spansih speaking countries (which are quite a
few...). Shall we ask Carol about this beforehand? I guess that
submissions will have to be in English...

Best,

Virgilio
